page.layout: One page of verse, one block, set in the centre-left of the scan. No running head, no margin notes. The catchword "Per-" stands alone at the lower right. Faint show-through from the facing page at the right edge is ignored.

p.i: Noctiuagum[?] minuit nitorem. Non astra casus instabiles rotant, Brutaq; sortis turbidus impetus: At illa iugi Lege fixus Ordo rapit, seriesq; ue certa. Et dextra summi Numinis aerem, Motusque cunctos temperat: hinc vice Venti stupenda per liquentes Horrisoni variantur auras. Nec casus imbrem format, & vberes Foecundat agros. Non tonat Impotens Fortuna: nec fulgur, grandinesq;: Aut rutila iaculatur arce Quos horret ignes impietas ferox, Parcusq; Diuum cultor, & infrequens: Quum pallet incertus, nigrisq; Sub specubus latitare quaerit, Audire tristes non patiens sonos Coeli ruentis, fulminis & feri Diros fragores, siue turres, Siue quatit crepitante flamma Sublimiorum culmina montium. Vt quum Sodomae subruit impias Coeleste gentes sulphur, atque Turpe simul scelus expiauit. Et, quae feraci cuncta fouet sinu, Tellus potentes pendula suspicit Nutus parentis, qui suprema

page.notes: Line 1: "Noctiuagum" is hard to read at the top of the line (ct ligature); reading is likely but not certain. The sign over "Brutaq;", "parcusq;", "nigrisq;", "grandinesq;" is a 3-shaped mark for -que, written as q;. "Coeleste" contains a Cyrillic-looking letter in my first draft; the word is Latin "Coeleste", written in Latin letters. The printed "sulphur" is copied as "sulphur". The verse appears to continue without stanza breaks; it is kept as one paragraph. The text continues on the next page ("Per-").
